offence_severity: Life imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 10,000/- and in default, further undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year. Rigorous imprisonment for five years and a fine of Rs. 5,000/- and in default, further undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months.
physical_harm: Injuries or death caused, briefly: The kidnapped boy was robbed of his wrist watch, ATM card, school card, gold chain and some money. He was blindfolded and threatened with elimination if the police were informed.
number_of_offences: Seven accused persons were charged, but four were finally upheld for offences punishable under Sections 364A, 392 and 120B IPC.
financial_property_loss: Money or property lost: Currency notes to the tune of Rs. 17,00,000/-, Rs. 3,50,000/-, Rs. 18,50,000/-, Rs. 20,00,000/-, Rs. 22,000/-, Rs. 20,50,000/-, Rs. 1,28,000/-, Rs. 40,000/- and other items were recovered.
premeditation_planning: The court found that the prosecution failed to establish premeditation or planning, and the case was deemed fabricated.
motive: The motive alleged was ransom, but the court found the prosecution's story to be fabricated and the accused framed for ulterior motives.
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the entire prosecution story was totally concocted and did not inspire confidence, with inherent improbabilities in the versions of the two star prosecution witnesses.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as unreliable, noting that the prosecution failed to examine the most relevant witness, the grandfather of the kidnapped boy, and that the identification of the accused by the boy was not free from doubt.

legal_representation.accused: Ms. Kiran Suri, Neeraj Kumar Jain, Sr. Advs., Ms. Bharti Tyagi, Vikash Kumar, T. N. Singh, Vikas Kumar Singh, Ms. Rajshree Singh, T. Mahipal, Advs.
legal_representation.state: S. Udaya Kumar Sagar, A.A.G., Ms. Bina Madhavan, Dr. Monika Gusain, Advs.

investigation_status: FIR registered on 15th April, 2003; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Non-examination of the most relevant witness, non-production of case property, registration of FIR based on secret information without verification, disposal of property without court order

appeal_history.supreme_court: Quashed and set aside the judgments, acquitted the appellants

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants kidnapped a minor boy for ransom and robbed him, with the ransom amount of Rs. One crore. The FIR was registered based on secret information received by the police, and the trial court and High Court upheld the conviction and sentence of the appellants.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution's story was fabricated and did not inspire confidence. The defence highlighted inherent improbabilities in the prosecution's witnesses' versions, the failure to examine the most relevant witness (the grandfather), and the lack of convincing evidence linking the accused to the suspected mobile numbers.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that courts must not act as mere spectators and must proactively participate in trial proceedings to ensure all relevant evidence is brought to light, especially when the prosecution fails to do so.
precedent_relied_upon: Pooja Pal v. Union of India and Others [2016] 11 SCR 560 : (2016) 3 SCC 135; Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal and Ors. [2020] 7 SCR 180 : (2020) 3 SCC 216
